section_1.title: Introduction: Fermat's Principle
section_1.content: Introduce the core intuition: Light travels between two points along the path that takes the least time. Hook: Why does a lifeguard run on sand but swim in water at an angle to reach a drowning swimmer fastest?
section_1.example: A lifeguard on a beach (slow medium) aiming for a swimmer in the ocean (fast medium) must choose a path that balances distance and speed.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Setup: Geometric Geometry
section_2.content: Define the interface between two media (n1, n2). Set up coordinates: Point A in medium 1, Point B in medium 2. Define the path distance x as a function of the angle of incidence (θ1) and refraction (θ2).
section_2.example: Visual: A coordinate grid over the interface. Light ray travels through point (0, h1) to (x, 0) and then to (L, -h2).

section_3.title: Formulating the Time Function
section_3.content: Construct the total time equation T(x) = (d1/v1) + (d2/v2), where distances are expressed as hypotenuses (sqrt(h^2 + x^2)). Explain that minimizing time is equivalent to taking the derivative and setting it to zero.

section_4.title: Calculus Derivation
section_4.content: Differentiate T(x) with respect to x. Set dT/dx = 0. Show the transition from the derivative expression to the sine components: x/sqrt(h^2 + x^2) = sin(θ).
section_4.example: Animation showing the derivative slope flattening out to zero at the optimal 'x' point.

section_5.title: Conclusion: The Final Law
section_5.content: Simplify the resulting algebraic expression into n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Reinforce how this proves that light 'pre-calculates' the path to minimize duration.
section_5.example: Summary graphic: A laser pointer hitting a glass block, with the calculated angles overlaying the geometric proof.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Setup: Geometric Geometry", [
            "Define the interface between two media.",
            "Place points A and B on either side.",
            "Map the light ray path coordinates."
        ])
        
        # Interface elements
        interface = Line(start=self.grid["D1"], end=self.grid["D6"], color="#33FF57")
        pt_a = Dot(color=WHITE)
        pt_b = Dot(color=WHITE)
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(interface))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33FF57")
